summary: Gate verdict: proceed_with_review. The change is highly verifiable (proposal, design with six numbered decisions, WHEN/THEN delta spec adding scenarios skill-workflow.12-14, test-first tasks.md with per-task design-decision and scenario references, contracts README, one scoped work package with four command-level verification steps; `openspec validate --strict` passes). Risk is low and fully reversible: 260 LOC across a local CLI driver, a new pure-function shared module, and test files; no database, no security surface, no external dependencies, no schema or payload change, write scope fenced to skills/{shared,audit-choices,prioritize-proposals}, their test trees, docs/guides/workflow.md and the change dir, with openspec/specs/** and agent-coordinator/** denied. The `has_db_migration: true` gate signal is confirmed a FALSE POSITIVE: the only 'migrat*' occurrences in the artifacts refer to migrating a Python module onto a shared helper (work-packages.yaml lines 28 and 33, design.md 'Migration Plan'); contracts/README.md states no schema is introduced or modified and no database, SQL, or ORM reference exists anywhere in the change. VAL_REVIEW is retained not for the false signal but for the one real risk: the change refactors prioritize-proposals, a second working skill, to fix a bug in audit-choices.
completed_work: Read all six planning artifacts on the feature branch worktree: proposal.md, design.md, tasks.md, specs/skill-workflow/spec.md, contracts/README.md, work-packages.yaml.

Assessed VERIFIABILITY: gate_signals has_specs/has_tasks/has_proposal/has_work_packages all true and confirmed against the artifacts themselves. The delta spec modifies one requirement and adds three scenarios with explicit THEN/AND clauses (range pair written outside openspec/changes/, change-id form byte-for-byte unchanged, retention archives rather than deletes). Every implementation task carries Spec scenarios and/or Design decisions plus an explicit Files list, and five phase checkpoints name runnable pytest/gate commands.

Assessed RISK: single sequential work package, loc_estimate 260, isolated worktree, verification tier B with four command steps (three skill suites, install.sh --check, dependency_direction linter, ci_coverage guard). Rollback is a revert of the shared module plus restoring two call sites; no on-disk artifact format changes, so already-written ledgers and reports stay valid either way.

Independently verified the factual claims the plan rests on: run_audit.py still derives change_dir from the raw change_id at the cited site; skills/shared/ exists and is declared under shared_libraries in skills/install-manifest.json, so no cross_skill_dependencies entry is needed as the design asserts; both skills/tests/shared/ and skills/tests/prioritize-proposals/ already exist, so no unregistered test directory is being introduced.
decisions: Verdict proceed_with_review rather than proceed: the plan deliberately refactors a working, unrelated skill (prioritize-proposals) to fix a defect in audit-choices. Design D4 mitigates this with a characterization test written before anything moves, and task 1.1 plus the Phase 3 checkpoint enforce that the test must pass unchanged afterwards. That is the right mitigation, and the extra VAL_REVIEW phase is the right place to confirm it was actually honoured rather than adjusted.

Verdict is not escalate: outcomes are objectively checkable, blast radius is three skill directories plus one docs file, and every effect is a file-location change that git revert undoes. Autopilot's downstream safeguards (multi-vendor PLAN/IMPL review convergence, VALIDATE, and the mandatory human merge gate) are more than adequate for this profile.

has_db_migration is dismissed as a substring false positive, verified directly rather than taken from the INIT note. Confirmed that VAL_REVIEW remains enabled for the refactor risk, which is independent of that signal.
next_steps: Proceed to the PLAN review phase with val_review_enabled left true.

Reviewers should give particular weight to the ordering constraint in tasks.md: the prioritize-proposals characterization test (1.1) must be committed and green against unmodified code before the shared module (2.2) or the migration (3.1) lands.

At VAL_REVIEW, confirm the characterization test's assertions were not weakened and that prioritize-proposals' on-disk output is byte-for-byte identical (run directory name, report.{md,json}, latest.*, archive destination).
Confirm the work package's scope fence held: nothing written under openspec/specs/** or agent-coordinator/**, and the new openspec/choices/ tree is the only new tracked tree.
